entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Johann Pfeffinger (1550-1573) was a prominent theologian and Protestant Reformer who played a pivotal role in shaping the religious landscape of Western Europe during the tumultuous 16th century. Born in the Holy Roman Empire, Pfeffinger's early life and education were marked by his involvement with various theological circles, which eventually led to his affiliation with the emerging Lutheran movement. His magnum opus, 'Theological Treatise on Justification,' published posthumously in 1575, solidified his reputation as a leading figure in the Protestant Reformation. Pfeffinger's influence extended beyond his own community, as he engaged in debates and dialogues with prominent Catholic theologians, including Peter Canisius. His commitment to ecumenical dialogue and reform contributed significantly to the ongoing dialogue between Lutherans and Catholics during this period. Theological debates surrounding justification, free will, and sacraments formed the backdrop of Pfeffinger's theological work, which has been widely studied and debated by scholars ever since. Through his influential writings and personal interactions with other prominent thinkers, Johann Pfeffinger left an enduring legacy in the annals of Protestant Reformation history.
